```diff
+ #!/bin/bash
+ # Server Port Management Helper Script
+ # Check and manage processes using port 8000 (or other ports)
+ 
+ # Colors for output
+ RED=&#39;\033[0;31m&#39;
+ GREEN=&#39;\033[0;32m&#39;
+ YELLOW=&#39;\033[1;33m&#39;
+ BLUE=&#39;\033[0;34m&#39;
+ NC=&#39;\033[0m&#39; # No Color
+ 
+ # Default port
+ PORT=&quot;${2:-8000}&quot;
+ 
+ # Function to print colored output
+ print_info() {
+     echo -e &quot;${BLUE}[INFO]${NC} $1&quot;
+ }
+ 
+ print_success() {
+     echo -e &quot;${GREEN}[SUCCESS]${NC} $1&quot;
+ }
+ 
+ print_warning() {
+     echo -e &quot;${YELLOW}[WARNING]${NC} $1&quot;
+ }
+ 
+ print_error() {
+     echo -e &quot;${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1&quot;
+ }
+ 
+ # Function to check if port is in use
+ check_port() {
+     local port=&quot;$1&quot;
+     
+     print_info &quot;Checking if port $port is in use...&quot;
+     
+     # Try to find process using the port
+     if command -v lsof &amp;&gt; /dev/null; then
+         local pid=$(lsof -ti:$port 2&gt;/dev/null)
+         if [ -n &quot;$pid&quot; ]; then
+             print_warning &quot;Port $port is in use!&quot;
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Process details:&quot;
+             lsof -i:$port
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Process ID (PID): $pid&quot;
+             return 0
+         else
+             print_success &quot;Port $port is available&quot;
+             return 1
+         fi
+     elif command -v netstat &amp;&gt; /dev/null; then
+         local pid=$(netstat -tlnp 2&gt;/dev/null | grep &quot;:$port &quot; | awk &#39;{print $7}&#39; | cut -d&#39;/&#39; -f1 | head -n1)
+         if [ -n &quot;$pid&quot; ]; then
+             print_warning &quot;Port $port is in use!&quot;
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Process details:&quot;
+             netstat -tlnp 2&gt;/dev/null | grep &quot;:$port &quot;
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Process ID (PID): $pid&quot;
+             return 0
+         else
+             print_success &quot;Port $port is available&quot;
+             return 1
+         fi
+     elif command -v ss &amp;&gt; /dev/null; then
+         local pid=$(ss -tlnp 2&gt;/dev/null | grep &quot;:$port &quot; | grep -oP &#39;pid=\K[0-9]+&#39; | head -n1)
+         if [ -n &quot;$pid&quot; ]; then
+             print_warning &quot;Port $port is in use!&quot;
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Process details:&quot;
+             ss -tlnp 2&gt;/dev/null | grep &quot;:$port &quot;
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Process ID (PID): $pid&quot;
+             return 0
+         else
+             print_success &quot;Port $port is available&quot;
+             return 1
+         fi
+     else
+         print_error &quot;No suitable command found (lsof, netstat, or ss). Cannot check port.&quot;
+         return 2
+     fi
+ }
+ 
+ # Function to kill process on port
+ kill_port() {
+     local port=&quot;$1&quot;
+     local force=&quot;${2:-false}&quot;
+     
+     print_info &quot;Attempting to kill process on port $port...&quot;
+     
+     # Find PID using the port
+     local pid=&quot;&quot;
+     
+     if command -v lsof &amp;&gt; /dev/null; then
+         pid=$(lsof -ti:$port 2&gt;/dev/null)
+     elif command -v netstat &amp;&gt; /dev/null; then
+         pid=$(netstat -tlnp 2&gt;/dev/null | grep &quot;:$port &quot; | awk &#39;{print $7}&#39; | cut -d&#39;/&#39; -f1 | head -n1)
+     elif command -v ss &amp;&gt; /dev/null; then
+         pid=$(ss -tlnp 2&gt;/dev/null | grep &quot;:$port &quot; | grep -oP &#39;pid=\K[0-9]+&#39; | head -n1)
+     else
+         print_error &quot;No suitable command found (lsof, netstat, or ss). Cannot kill process.&quot;
+         return 1
+     fi
+     
+     if [ -z &quot;$pid&quot; ]; then
+         print_warning &quot;No process found using port $port&quot;
+         return 1
+     fi
+     
+     # Show process info before killing
+     print_info &quot;Found process: PID $pid&quot;
+     ps -p &quot;$pid&quot; -o pid,ppid,cmd --no-headers 2&gt;/dev/null || print_warning &quot;Could not get process details&quot;
+     
+     if [ &quot;$force&quot; != &quot;true&quot; ]; then
+         echo &quot;&quot;
+         read -p &quot;Kill this process? (y/N): &quot; -n 1 -r
+         echo &quot;&quot;
+         if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
+             print_info &quot;Cancelled&quot;
+             return 1
+         fi
+     fi
+     
+     # Kill the process
+     kill &quot;$pid&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null
+     
+     # Wait a moment and check if it&#39;s still running
+     sleep 1
+     if ps -p &quot;$pid&quot; &gt; /dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
+         print_warning &quot;Process still running, trying force kill...&quot;
+         kill -9 &quot;$pid&quot; 2&gt;/dev/null
+         sleep 1
+         if ps -p &quot;$pid&quot; &gt; /dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
+             print_error &quot;Failed to kill process $pid&quot;
+             return 1
+         fi
+     fi
+     
+     print_success &quot;Process $pid killed successfully&quot;
+     return 0
+ }
+ 
+ # Function to start server safely (check and kill if needed, then start)
+ start_server() {
+     local port=&quot;${1:-8000}&quot;
+     
+     print_info &quot;Starting server on port $port...&quot;
+     
+     # Check if port is in use
+     if check_port &quot;$port&quot; &gt; /dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
+         print_warning &quot;Port $port is in use. Attempting to free it...&quot;
+         kill_port &quot;$port&quot; &quot;true&quot;
+     fi
+     
+     # Wait a moment for port to be freed
+     sleep 1
+     
+     # Double check
+     if check_port &quot;$port&quot; &gt; /dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1; then
+         print_error &quot;Port $port is still in use. Please check manually.&quot;
+         return 1
+     fi
+     
+     print_success &quot;Port $port is available. Starting server...&quot;
+     
+     # Change to admin directory and start server
+     cd &quot;/var/www/projectmanager.test/github_v2/admin&quot; || {
+         print_error &quot;Could not change to admin directory&quot;
+         return 1
+     }
+     
+     # Check if venv exists and activate it
+     if [ -f &quot;venv/bin/activate&quot; ]; then
+         source venv/bin/activate
+     else
+         print_warning &quot;Virtual environment not found. Make sure it&#39;s set up.&quot;
+     fi
+     
+     # Start uvicorn
+     uvicorn app:app --reload --port &quot;$port&quot; --host 127.0.0.1
+ }
+ 
+ # Main function
+ main() {
+     case &quot;$1&quot; in
+         &quot;check&quot;)
+             check_port &quot;$PORT&quot;
+             ;;
+         &quot;kill&quot;)
+             kill_port &quot;$PORT&quot;
+             ;;
+         &quot;start&quot;)
+             start_server &quot;$PORT&quot;
+             ;;
+         *)
+             echo &quot;Server Port Management Helper&quot;
+             echo &quot;============================&quot;
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Usage: $0 &lt;command&gt; [port]&quot;
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Commands:&quot;
+             echo &quot;  check [port]    Check if port is in use (default: 8000)&quot;
+             echo &quot;  kill [port]     Kill process using port (default: 8000)&quot;
+             echo &quot;  start [port]    Check, kill if needed, and start server (default: 8000)&quot;
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Examples:&quot;
+             echo &quot;  $0 check        # Check port 8000&quot;
+             echo &quot;  $0 check 8001   # Check port 8001&quot;
+             echo &quot;  $0 kill         # Kill process on port 8000&quot;
+             echo &quot;  $0 kill 8001    # Kill process on port 8001&quot;
+             echo &quot;  $0 start        # Start server on port 8000 (auto-kill if needed)&quot;
+             echo &quot;&quot;
+             echo &quot;Note: The &#39;start&#39; command will:&quot;
+             echo &quot;  1. Check if the port is in use&quot;
+             echo &quot;  2. Kill the process if it is&quot;
+             echo &quot;  3. Start uvicorn server in the admin directory&quot;
+             ;;
+     esac
+ }
+ 
+ # Run main function with all arguments
+ main &quot;$@&quot;
+ 
```

Created a server helper script. Summary:

## Created `server-helper.sh`

The script provides three commands:

1. **Check port status:**
   ```bash
   ./server-helper.sh check
   ```
   Shows if port 8000 is in use and which process is using it.

2. **Kill process on port:**
   ```bash
   ./server-helper.sh kill
   ```
   Prompts for confirmation, then kills the process using port 8000.

3. **Start server automatically:**
   ```bash
   ./server-helper.sh start
   ```
   Checks if the port is in use, kills the process if needed, then starts the uvicorn server.

### Features:
- Works with `lsof`, `netstat`, or `ss` (uses whichever is available)
- Colored output for readability
- Supports custom ports: `./server-helper.sh check 8001`
- Safe killing with confirmation (unless using `start` command)
- Automatically activates the virtual environment when starting the server

### Usage Examples:

```bash
# Check if port 8000 is in use
./server-helper.sh check

# Kill whatever is using port 8000
./server-helper.sh kill

# Start server (auto-checks and kills if needed)
./server-helper.sh start
```

The script is executable and ready to use. The README has been updated with these instructions. When switching computers and the port is still in use, run `./server-helper.sh kill` before starting the server, or use `./server-helper.sh start` to handle it automatically.

## Changes Made:

1. **Added database connection timeouts** (10 seconds) to all SQLite connections to prevent indefinite hangs when the database is locked.

2. **Optimized `ensure_tech_skills_categories()`**:
   - Added caching so it only runs once per server session
   - Uses a context manager for proper connection handling
   - Avoids running on every API request

3. **Updated all database connection functions** to include timeouts:
   - `get_conn()`
   - `get_doc_conn()`
   - `get_ref_conn()`
   - `get_tech_skills_conn()`
   - `get_side_projects_conn()`
   - `get_magento_conn()`
   - `get_photography_conn()`
   - `get_experience_conn()`

## Next Steps:

Restart the server to apply the changes. If it's running with `--reload`, it should auto-reload, but a manual restart ensures it:

```bash
# Kill the current server
./server-helper.sh kill

# Start it again
./server-helper.sh start
```

These changes should:
- Prevent the admin dashboard from hanging (timeout prevents indefinite waits)
- Speed up the tech-skills API endpoint (cached category check)
- Improve overall database connection handling

After restarting, test:
1. Access `http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin` — should load without hanging
2. Load `http://githubv2.projectmanager.test/index.html` — tech-skills and references should load faster

If issues persist, check the server logs for specific errors.

## Summary of Fixes:

### 1. **Fixed `server-helper.sh` to handle multiple PIDs**
   - Previously only handled a single PID
   - Now loops through all PIDs using the port
   - Kills all processes (uvicorn spawns child processes)
   - Improved feedback showing how many processes were found/killed
   - Added retry logic with longer waits for port availability

### 2. **Database connection improvements** (from earlier)
   - Added 10-second timeouts to all SQLite connections
   - Optimized `ensure_tech_skills_categories()` with caching
   - Prevents indefinite hangs when databases are locked

## Server Status:
- Server is running on port 8000 (PIDs: 4391, 4396)
- Port management script is working correctly
- Database timeout fixes are active

You can now:
1. Access `http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin` — should load without hanging
2. Load `http://githubv2.projectmanager.test/index.html` — tech-skills and references should load faster

The script will now properly handle killing all processes when you switch computers. Use:
- `./server-helper.sh kill` - to kill all processes on port 8000
- `./server-helper.sh start` - to automatically kill and restart the server
- `./server-helper.sh check` - to check port status

Test the admin panel and frontend to confirm the performance improvements.

Server is running and listening on all interfaces (`0.0.0.0:8000`). Summary of fixes:

## Fixes Applied:

### 1. **Server Binding** (`server-helper.sh`)
   - Changed from `--host 127.0.0.1` to `--host 0.0.0.0`
   - Server now accepts connections from any network interface, not just localhost

### 2. **Frontend API URLs** (`index.html`)
   - Changed from hardcoded `http://127.0.0.1:8000` to dynamic `${window.location.protocol}//${host}:8000`
   - When accessing via `githubv2.projectmanager.test`, API calls go to `http://githubv2.projectmanager.test:8000` instead of `127.0.0.1:8000`
   - Avoids browser security issues with mixed origins

### 3. **Database Connection Improvements** (from earlier)
   - Added 10-second timeouts to prevent hangs
   - Optimized tech skills category initialization

## Current Status:
- Server is running on port 8000, listening on all interfaces
- Frontend will use the same hostname for API calls
- Database connections have proper timeouts

## Next Steps:
1. Refresh your browser (hard refresh: Ctrl+Shift+R or Cmd+Shift+R)
2. Test accessing:
   - Frontend: `http://githubv2.projectmanager.test/index.html`
   - Backend: `http://githubv2.projectmanager.test:8000/admin`

If it still doesn't work, check:
- Browser console for errors (F12 → Console)
- Network tab to see if requests are being made
- Firewall/proxy settings that might block port 8000

The server should now be accessible from the domain name.
